report:
### Conclusion
**Yes**, clinical evidence indicates that monk’s pepper (*Vitex agnus-castus*, also known as chasteberry) can help reduce premenstrual syndrome (PMS) symptoms.

### Evidence Summary
* **Clinical Efficacy:** Meta-analyses of double-blind, randomized controlled trials demonstrate that standardized *Vitex agnus-castus* extracts significantly alleviate PMS symptoms compared to placebos (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229919306053).
* **Symptom Relief:** Monk's pepper is recognized for reducing both physical and psychological PMS complaints, including cycle-related breast pain and tenderness (https://endometriose.app/en/insights/does-monks-pepper-help-with-endometriosis-2/, https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/chasteberry).
* **Safety & Tolerability:** Randomized clinical trials show that monk's pepper extract is a safe, well-tolerated, and effective option for treating moderate to severe PMS (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19269753/).
* **Proposed Mechanism:** It is thought to influence the hormonal system via the pituitary gland, though the precise biological mechanisms are still being established (https://endometriose.app/en/insights/does-monks-pepper-help-with-endometriosis-2/).
